## The Dead Wood

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_10_the_dead_wood.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_10_the_dead_wood.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** aldric · **Turn-in:** lastchampion

**Follows:** `quest_main_09_the_kingsworn`

### title

The Dead Wood

### summary

Below the halls is the king's own ground: a wood with nothing living in it and a road running up to a barrow. A champion of the Order sits at the foot of the stair and has sat there since long before Aldric's watch. She is the last person who will tell you anything.

### offer_line

Last thing I can give you, and it is only words. 

Down there is his own ground. A wood with nothing living in it and a road running up to a barrow, and he is on the barrow. 

There is a champion sitting at the bottom of the stair. She has been there since long before my watch and she does not get up. 

Go to her first. Every one of us who got that far did, and every one of us came back knowing something we did not know going in.

### accept_option

I'll go down.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

Don't be unsettled by her. She is further along than the rest of us, that's all.

### refused_line

Then the stair waits. It is very good at that.

### reoffer_line

Down the stair when you are ready. Will you go?

### progress_line

She is at the bottom, against a dead tree, to your left.

### continue_option

I'm going.

### abandon_option

Not yet.

### abandoned_line

Take the fire for a while. Nobody here will say a word.

### complete_line

You made it. She says it without much interest, and does not look up. 

He is up the road, past the pillars, on the barrow, and there are two things standing in the glades either side of the road between here and there. 

One is the knight who let you past the altar and one is the knight who stepped aside in the stair, He imagined them here, because four hundred years alone with what he had done left him reaching for the only two people in the world he could still trust, 

and he set one either side of his road so that he would not have to be the only thing down here.

### done_line
She keeps that stair. She has kept it for every one of us.

## The King in the Barrow

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_13_the_king_in_the_barrow.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_13_the_king_in_the_barrow.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** lastchampion

**Follows:** `quest_main_10_the_dead_wood`

**Recommended level:** 38 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

The King in the Barrow

### summary

Up the road, past the glades and the pillars, the barrow. He cannot be killed. He was never meant to be. He can be put down hard enough and long enough for the rite to close over him, and then he sleeps, and that is the whole of the victory and always has been.

### offer_line

You cannot kill him. Nobody can. That is not the Order failing and it is not you failing; it is the bargain, and the god of the dead does not take returns. 

What you can do is put him down hard enough he sleeps once more. 

That is the whole victory. A brief respite for a kind king that is a mere shell now.

### accept_option

I'll put him under.

### refuse_option

Not yet.

### accepted_line

He is waiting for you, like he have done for the countless others before you. Do not fail him. Give him the respite he desires.

### refused_line

Do not keep him waiting too long. 

### reoffer_line

 He is on the barrow surrounded only be dead.

### progress_line

Up the road, past the pillars. The stone first, then him. I will not come and watch.

### continue_option

I'm going back up.

### abandon_option

I can't do it.

### abandoned_line

Mm. Go back down to the fire and let Aldric look pleased about it. He will be, you know. He will be glad you came back.

### complete_line

It has gone quiet. Look at the wood, champion. Look at it. I have sat under this tree for longer than your town has stood and yet each time it happens I cannot help but marvel.

### done_line

Go up, champion. you have laid him to a peaceful slumber. Thank you.

### caution_line

The Last Champion: Below level %d I would not go up that barrow. I went up it at less, and you can see how that ended.
